summary.prose: When the reader of a Claude turn is abandoned before the turn's result (the chat is detached, you switch chats, or the follow is stopped), the adapter now ends the CLI's input in run()'s finally. The CLI then finishes its in-flight work and exits by itself, so it no longer idles holding the session's chat lock. Nothing closes the input at spawn or before the result, and the background observer is unchanged.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Standalone feature — no parent HLD. Design directly against the repo, grounded on the s1 analyze passes. There are no HLD shared contracts to honour.

boundary.internal: End a correlated Claude turn's stdin when its reader is abandoned

api.name: run
api.signature: run(req: TurnRequest, opts?: RunOptions): AsyncIterable<TurnEvent>  // existing method of makeStreamAdapter, finally extended

parameters.name: opts
parameters.purpose: Spawn, progress and decoder hooks; unchanged.

returns.meaning: Unchanged: the turn's events, ending at a done or error.

preconditions: The turn is a correlated Claude turn (the mapper has formatInput, so state.requestUuid is defined).
postconditions: If the iterator is abandoned before a terminal event, the CLI's input is ended in the finally, once, before any pipe-turn kill.
If a terminal event was reached, the finally adds nothing: the input was already ended in the read loop.
A pipe turn that is abandoned is still stopped with SIGTERM and its pending requests are cleared, as before.
Codex and Vibe turns (no requestUuid) are untouched.

api.name: endInput
api.signature: endInput?(): void  // existing optional member of SpawnedProcess

returns.meaning: Ends the process stdin; idempotent and never throws.

postconditions: A second call, or a call on a destroyed or ended stream, does nothing.

dataModelChanges.details: Before: a Claude turn that writes to its session file and is abandoned before its result is only detached from, so its input stays open and the CLI idles after its answer. After: the input is ended when the reader is abandoned before the result. The input is never ended earlier than that, and the observer takes no action on the process. The current behaviour that is kept: the CLI's pid, the live entry and the pending requests are released by the process's exit, not by the stream.

errorCases.scenario: The process seam's endInput() throws when called from the finally
errorCases.detection: The call in the finally raises an exception (the production seam is guarded, but a test double or another spawner need not be).
errorCases.response: The call is wrapped so the exception is swallowed and the rest of the finally (pipe-turn kill, pending-request cleanup) still runs.
errorCases.userImpact: None: the cleanup the finally already did is not skipped.

errorCases.scenario: The CLI does not exit after its input ended
errorCases.detection: proc.exit stays unresolved after the abandonment; the adapter does not watch for it.
errorCases.response: No new action: the live map entry stays until exit, and cancel() and the stop paths remain the way to end it.
errorCases.userImpact: The chat lock stays held until the user stops the turn, as for any turn that does not finish.

errorCases.scenario: An in-turn approval is pending when the reader is abandoned
errorCases.detection: A later decide() finds the stdin ended: the process seam's write() returns false for an ended stream.
errorCases.response: decide() reports delivered false and does not consume the request, so the existing follow-up path answers it.
errorCases.userImpact: The approval is answered by a follow-up run instead of over the closed pipe.

edgeCases.input: The reader is abandoned after the correlated result
edgeCases.expected: The input was already ended in the read loop; the finally sees terminal true and adds no second call.

edgeCases.input: The reader is abandoned while a read is pending and the next line is the result
edgeCases.expected: The generator resumes, handles the result (ending the input there) and the finally then does nothing more.

edgeCases.input: The reader is abandoned while a read is pending and the next line is not the result

edgeCases.input: A Codex or Vibe turn is abandoned
edgeCases.expected: No request id and no endInput: nothing is called.

edgeCases.input: A pipe turn (no session output) is abandoned before its result

invariantsToPreserve.text: The input is ended at the correlated result inside the read loop, exactly once, and never before it.
An abandoned pipe turn is stopped with SIGTERM and its pending requests are cleared; a session-file turn is not killed.
The live entry and the pending requests are released by the process's exit, not by the stream.
endInput stays optional and idempotent on the process seam, and its production implementation guards destroyed and ended streams.
The production implementation of endInput stays input.end() behind the destroyed and writableEnded guards.
Abandoning an iterator stays a non-waiting return(); the lifecycle is not changed.
Detach keeps leaving the CLI writing to the session file for the observer to finish.
The observer still reads detached turns and takes no action on the process.

migration.stateBefore: A correlated Claude turn's input is ended only in run()'s read loop at the correlated result (cli-adapter.ts:1322); a session-file turn abandoned earlier is only detached from (cli-adapter.ts:1375-1384), so the CLI idles after its answer and holds the chat lock.
migration.stateAfter: run()'s finally also ends the input of a correlated turn that is abandoned before its result, so the CLI finishes its in-flight work and exits by itself. Nothing closes the input earlier, and the observer is unchanged.

migrationSteps.action: Add the abandonment branch to run()'s finally: for a correlated turn with no terminal event, end the input before the existing pipe-turn kill, shielding the rest of the cleanup from a throwing seam.
Add the unit tests for abandonment, no-early-close and the throwing seam to the correlation suite.
Record the live checks as reported test results in the build's test record.

migration.backwardCompat: No public API, wire format, stored record or setting changes. endInput stays an optional member of the process seam; spawners without it behave as before.

alternativesConsidered.name: End the input in run()'s finally when a correlated turn is abandoned before its result
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: In run()'s existing finally, call the existing endInput() seam when the turn is correlated and no terminal event was reached.
alternativesConsidered.approach: In run()'s finally (cli-adapter.ts:1375-1384), add one branch: when state.requestUuid is defined and 'terminal' is still false, call proc.endInput?.() before the existing pipe-turn kill. endInput() is already idempotent and never throws (it checks destroyed and writableEnded), so a later normal terminal path or a second call is harmless. A turn that reached its terminal has already ended its input in the read loop, so the finally changes nothing for it. A session-file turn is then left to finish its in-flight work and exit by itself (live check: it completes the turn, answers with the matching request id, exits 0, and lets background tasks finish); a pipe turn is still killed as today. Nothing closes the input at spawn or before the correlated result, and the observer is unchanged. Codex and Vibe have no endInput and are untouched.
pros: One branch in one function; reuses the endInput() seam and its guards
Covers every way the reader is abandoned (detach, switching chats, stop-follow, supersession) because they all end in the finally
Matches the measured CLI behaviour: finishing in-flight work, then exit 0, with background tasks allowed to finish
No change to the lifecycle, the panel, the observer or the process seam
cons: Depends on the generator's finally running: a return() made while a read is pending takes effect after that read settles, so closing waits for the next output line or the end of output
A pending in-turn approval can no longer be answered over this process's stdin once the input is closed (it falls to the follow-up path that already exists)

alternativesConsidered.name: Give the lifecycle an explicit handle to end the input at detach
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: Expose endInput on the TurnProcess handle passed to onSpawn and have the lifecycle's detach and stop call it directly.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Add an optional endInput() to the TurnProcess handle that run() passes to opts.onSpawn, and have turn-lifecycle.ts call it in detachThis and the other places that abandon a live iterator, instead of relying on run()'s finally. The adapter keeps its call at the correlated result.
pros: Closes the input at the moment of detach, independent of when the generator's finally runs
Makes the intent visible at the call sites in the lifecycle
cons: Widens the public TurnProcess contract and touches turn-lifecycle.ts at several abandon sites
Every present and future abandon site has to remember to call it; the finally covers them all
Needs matching changes in the test harness handles and the plugin's other TurnProcess consumers
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Closes at the exact moment of detach but widens the TurnProcess contract and every abandon site in the lifecycle for no gain the finally does not already give.

alternativesConsidered.name: Keep the input open and let a background watcher close it after the result
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: When the reader is abandoned, hand the process to a watcher that closes the input once the correlated result appears in the session file.
alternativesConsidered.approach: On abandonment, keep a watcher in the adapter that tails the session output for the correlated result of that turn and ends the input when it appears, so the CLI never sees EOF mid-turn.
pros: The CLI never sees EOF before its answer, so it cannot be affected by any EOF-in-the-middle behaviour
cons: Adds a second reader per detached turn beside the observer, with its own lifetime and error handling
The live check shows EOF mid-turn is safe, so the added machinery buys nothing
A watcher lost with the host leaves the same idle process this defect describes
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Adds a second reader per detached turn to avoid an EOF-in-the-middle risk that the live check shows does not exist.

alternativesConsidered.name: Close the input at spawn when no approvals can arrive
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: End stdin right after writing the user message for turns that cannot raise a permission request.
alternativesConsidered.approach: After the user message is written, end the input at once for permission modes where the CLI never asks the host, so the CLI exits at its own result without any later close.
pros: No dependence on the reader at all for those turns
cons: It is the preemptive closing the user ruled out
Does not help turns in review mode, which need stdin for decisions
Needs a reliable per-mode rule for when a request cannot arise, which the adapter does not have today
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Is the preemptive closing the user ruled out and cannot serve review-mode turns.
